findings.title: ShinyHunters: Cyber Criminal Group Attacks Learning Management System (IC3 PSA I-051526-PSA)
findings.summary_md: The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center warned that ShinyHunters attacked an online Learning Management System used by educational institutions and described the group's pressure tactics, including harassment, swatting, and false claims of possessing compromising material. This May 15 PSA is the report ShinyHunters later demanded the FBI withdraw or correct, making it the stated motive for the FBI job portal intrusion.

findings.title: Oracle Security Alert Advisory - CVE-2026-35273
findings.summary_md: Oracle's out-of-band Security Alert, initial release June 10, 2026, fixes CVE-2026-35273 in PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62, remotely exploitable without authentication over HTTP and leading to remote code execution, CVSS 9.8. The affected component is listed as Updates Environment Management. Credit for the report goes to researchers at TrendAI Zero Day Initiative and TrendAI Research.

findings.title: ShinyHunters Targets Education Sector with Oracle PeopleSoft Exploit
findings.summary_md: Mandiant and GTIG disclosed the original campaign: UNC6240 (ShinyHunters) exploited CVE-2026-35273 as a zero-day between May 27 and June 9, 2026, predating Oracle's June 10 advisory. The team notified over 100 organizations with correlated vulnerable endpoints, 68 percent of them higher education institutions, and documented MeshCentral staging infrastructure masquerading as Azure endpoints at azurenetfiles.net, a defacement marker file, zstd-packed exfiltration, and a June 9 leak site post. Open attacker staging directories on five 142.11.200.x hosts were flagged publicly on June 9.

findings.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog (CVE-2026-35273)
findings.summary_md: CISA added the exploited Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability CVE-2026-35273 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 12, 2026, two days after the Oracle patch, formalizing that the flaw was under active attack and triggering federal remediation deadlines.

findings.title: Cybergang ShinyHunters attackiert Oracle-PeopleSoft-Schwachstelle
findings.summary_md: Early coverage tying ShinyHunters to active attacks on the newly patched PeopleSoft flaw, citing Mandiant's finding that the group targeted PSEMHUB environment management endpoints worldwide. Recommended mitigations included restricting /PSEMHUB/* and /PSIGW/HttpListeningConnector to internal addresses, treating WAF rules as insufficient, and watching outbound traffic on port 445.

findings.title: ShinyHunters hackers say they breached Federal Bureau of Investigation
findings.summary_md: First news coverage of the claim: on Tuesday, September 22, ShinyHunters said it breached the FBI jobs portal at fbijobs.gov, citing anger over the FBI report that groups victims into sextortion categories and demanding retraction or correction within a week. Reuters matched sample records against credit bureau and prior leak data, with at least 10 matching including Director Kash Patel, and noted the samples carried names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, and duty assignments.

findings.title: Cybergang ShinyHunters behauptet Einbruch in FBI-Jobportal
findings.summary_md: Second-day coverage noting the ShinyHunters leak site no longer listed the FBI entry, the jobs portal remained offline, and an FBI statement left open whether the attackers hit a third party or FBI systems. It also recorded the group's reference to the May 2026 IC3 report as the trigger and its one-week ultimatum.

findings.title: ShinyHunters Renewed Mass Exploitation Campaign Targeting Oracle PeopleSoft
findings.summary_md: Mandiant and GTIG reported renewed mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273 by UNC6240 with expanded targeting across education, technology, healthcare, agriculture, transportation, and government, specifically hitting organizations that applied WAF rules but did not patch. The bypass requests /%50SEMHUB/ instead of /PSEMHUB/, defeating literal path-matching WAF rules; the post documents x.jsp and u.jsp web shells, the SIDEEYE backdoor delivered via a trojanized EV-signed Ple64.exe installer, Neo-reGeorg tunnels, MeshCentral agents, and C2 at 162.219.30.165 on TCP 3333 and 3334.

findings.title: Dutch Police Arrest 'Reformed' Hacker in Shiny Hunters Investigation
findings.summary_md: KrebsOnSecurity identified the arrested 24-year-old as Pepijn van der Stap, previously convicted in 2023 as Umbreon and detained on or around September 16, days before the group escalated with the FBI breach and the extortion of Cl0p. The piece links the group's risky pivot to new leadership under a teenager known as Rey of ScatteredLapsussHunters, cites a Mandiant estimate that ShinyHunters is on track for nearly 100 million dollars in 2026 extortion payments, and notes the suspect was due before the Rotterdam District Court on September 29.
